title: PM2 runs your ecosystem file AS AN APP unless its name contains `.config.` (e.g. `ecosystem.config.cjs`)
summary: A JavaScript ecosystem file is read as configuration only when its name contains `.config.`. `pm2 start deploy.cjs` launches deploy.cjs itself as a script named "deploy", and the apps it defines never start.
body_markdown:
## What happens (reproduced)
The same file, defining one app named `defined` with `instances: 2`, under two names:
- `pm2 start eco.cjs` → one process named **`eco`** running `eco.cjs` itself, fork mode. The app `defined` does not exist.
- `pm2 start eco.config.cjs` → two `defined` workers running the declared script.

## Fix
- Name ecosystem files `*.config.cjs` (or `.js`/`.mjs`).
- If a stray process appeared, delete it by name or id, then `pm2 save` so it does not come back at boot.
